title: Lior and the Spire
premise: Theo Dravenmoor has spent her life in the Valley of Ash, a place the old gods abandoned and magic cannot enter, working as a royal food-taster who builds immunity to poison one carefully dosed dish at a time. When prayers begin to be answered again and the king's behavior turns monstrous, Theo learns the crown itself is a vessel for a hungry god wearing her king like a coat. To unbind him she must leave the valley, trading the invisibility that kept her alive for a journey through a land where her suppressed memories—and her suppressed magic—are the only weapons that work. In the end she frees the king by giving the god what it truly wants: a witness to its original crime, and she pays for survival by letting the valley forget her name.
about_author: Tamsin Montrose is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging the private letters of minor nobility, an experience she describes as 'reading a hundred novels that never got finished.' She writes fantasy about people whose jobs history forgets, and lives in a drafty coastal house with too many clocks.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She samples the king's breakfast and detects almond in a soup that should have none, saving a chamberlain's life. The court barely notices her, which is exactly how she likes it. Emotional beat: the quiet pride of a woman whose survival depends on remaining unremarkable.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Ash Valley
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A shrine outside the city walls, dead for a century, begins to smoke. Pilgrims arrive claiming answered prayers; the king orders the shrine sealed. Theo, curious, touches the stone and hears her own name spoken in a voice she almost remembers. Emotional beat: unease—the past knocking.

chapters.title: The King Who Stopped Blinking
chapters.summary: Chamberlain Wren's POV. Wren observes the king at council: he no longer blinks, no longer eats, and his shadow moves a half-second behind him. Wren quietly adds Theo to the king's personal tasting roster, hoping her peculiar talents will reveal what his eyes cannot. Emotional beat: dawning dread dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Almond, Again
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Poison attempts multiply—three dishes in two days—yet the king consumes them untouched. Theo realizes no one is trying to kill the king; something inside him is testing the court. The sealed shrine burns in the distance. Emotional beat: the taster realizes she is tasting for a god, not a man.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo investigates her own immunity: her mother's letters reveal the valley was built to cage memory itself, and Theo was left there deliberately. The god in the king sends a dream offering to return what the valley took. Emotional beat: grief for a childhood she chose to forget.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Theo with evidence and a plan: get the king to the valley's border, where the crown's hold weakens. He offers her freedom papers; she names a higher price—the truth of who left her in the Ash Valley. Emotional beat: two cautious people deciding to trust.

chapters.title: The Road Out
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo leaves the valley for the first time in her life. Magic floods back like blood into a numb limb: she can taste intentions, hear lies as flavors. The first village they pass has hanged its priest for praying to the wrong old god. Emotional beat: vertigo and wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The God of Small Cruelties
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At a roadside inn, Theo tastes a cup of wine and tastes the god's signature—ash and almond. It speaks through a child, revealing it was bound once before, by a taster, and that taster was her mother. Emotional beat: the inheritance she never wanted, made undeniable.

chapters.title: Crown and Cage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren interrogates the court physician and learns the king has been 'dying' for a year, kept alive only by the crown's will. Unbinding the god may kill the king. Wren must choose between loyalty to a man and loyalty to a kingdom. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of mercy.

chapters.title: The Border of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They reach the valley's edge, where the king collapses as the god fights the dead magic. Theo touches the crown and experiences the god's memory: it was not a conqueror but a scapegoat, fed the kingdom's sins for centuries. Emotional beat: horror at realizing the monster was made, not born.

chapters.title: A Kingdom of Debt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Back at court, the queen regent's faction moves to declare the king dead and seize power. Wren is arrested for treason. His interrogation scene reveals the conspiracy fed the god deliberately, using it as a disposal for guilt. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institutions he served.

chapters.title: The Taster's Daughter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds her mother alive in exile, a former royal taster who bound the god decades ago at the cost of her own memories. Her mother warns: unbinding requires a witness willing to carry the god's whole memory, and it will hollow her. Emotional beat: reconciliation shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: Lessons in Bitterness
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Training montage of sorts: Theo learns to hold foreign memories without drowning, tasting each of the god's centuries of accumulated sin. She begins to lose her own small memories in trade—her teacher's face, the taste of her first meal. Emotional beat: the price of survival becoming literal.

chapters.title: The Empty Crown
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Freed by sympathizers, Wren returns to a capital where the god-king has begun public 'confession trials,' consuming the guilt of nobles and growing stronger. Wren realizes the plan must move now. Emotional beat: urgency and guilt—he built this machine's gears.

chapters.title: What the God Wants
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts the god directly in a dream and asks what it truly desires. Not worship, not freedom—an apology, a witness, someone to say: this was done to you, and it was wrong. No one has ever asked. Emotional beat: pity for the thing she must fight.

chapters.title: The Confession Trials
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The god-king puts Wren on trial, forcing him to confess his complicity before the court. Instead of breaking him, the confession cracks the court's silence—others begin admitting what they fed the crown. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, messy and human.

chapters.title: Ash and Almond
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo infiltrates the coronation anniversary feast as a taster, the one role no one guards against. She poisons the crown, not the king—a tincture of valley ash that deadens magic. The god, wounded, drags the court into shared memory. Emotional beat: the invisible woman made suddenly, terribly visible.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Climax. Before the assembled court, Theo takes the god's entire memory into herself and speaks its history aloud: the binding, the feeding, the centuries of borrowed guilt. The court weeps; the god, finally witnessed, loosens its grip. The king breathes on his own for the first time in a year. Emotional beat: catharsis through truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The god, unbound, offers to leave—but the memories must go somewhere. Theo carries them out of the valley and releases them to the old shrine, letting the land itself remember. She survives, but the valley's forgetting now includes her: her records, her name, her mother's letters, gone blank. Emotional beat: hollow triumph.

chapters.title: A King Who Blinks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The recovering king, frail and human, must face a court that saw everything. He abolishes the taster's office and the confession trials, founding instead a public archive of the god's testimony. Wren declines a promotion, choosing to rebuild the shrine instead. Emotional beat: institutions learning humility.

chapters.title: The Woman Without a Name
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo returns to the valley that no longer remembers her. She tastes the air, finds work in a kitchen, and begins writing her own memory down by hand—refusing to be erased entirely. A stranger asks her name; she hesitates, then chooses a new one. Emotional beat: quiet reclamation.

chapters.title: Lior and the Spire
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Years later, a girl apprentice finds Theo's handwritten memory-books hidden in the spire library and reads the first line: 'I was the taster.' Theo, old and at peace, watches the shrine smoke gently on the hill—no longer a prison, just a place to say thank you. Emotional beat: memory outlasting forgetting, on her own terms.
